verdicts.independent_reproduction: Q commutes with first-block symmetrization. Apply L1 to QT, use ||P QT||<=||PT||+delta and ||T||<=||QT||+delta to obtain binom(q,p)||PT||+(binom(q,p)+1)delta. The explicit antisymmetric p=1,q=2 tensor has squared norm 2 and projection 0.

verdicts.subject: w348 ATTEMPT.md L3
verdicts.exact_scope: Independent centered rate-one exponentials in any finite dimension; all f in L2; normalized ordered-index HS derivatives, d>=1.
verdicts.independent_reproduction: The normalized tilt kernel is product_i (1-z_i)exp(z_i Y_i). Its coefficients P_j=y^j/j!-y^(j-1)/(j-1)! are centered for j>=1 and have Gram coefficient binom(j+k-2,j-1). Ordered-index multiplicities give weight alpha!/d!. Different supports are orthogonal by independence and centering. Within support size s, the finite-rank frame trace is <=binom(2(d-s),d-s)*sum alpha!/d!<=binom(2d-2,d-1). The direct-sum norm is the maximum over support blocks, not their sum. f=P_d(Y_1)/sqrt(binom(2d-2,d-1)) attains equality. Central binomial upper/lower bounds imply optimal all-degree base 2.
verdicts.remaining_gap: Product independence is indispensable to this proof; the same direct-sum argument has not been proved for correlated log-concave laws. No full-target claim.

verdicts.subject: w349-C004
verdicts.independent_reproduction: Multiplying exp(-(x+1))1{x>=-1} by exp(x-tx^2/2) leaves a truncated Gaussian. For Z=sqrt(t)X the truncation is Z>=-sqrt(t). Dominated convergence of moments on [-1,infinity) gives mean sqrt(2/pi), second moment 1, variance 1-2/pi.
verdicts.remaining_gap: The worst-case endpoint theta=1 is paired with t>0. At t=0 its tilt is not normalizable. No localization expectation conclusion.

verdicts.subject: w349-C005
verdicts.independent_reproduction: Stopped Brownian Y_t is a bounded martingale in [-1/4,1/4]. diag(1+Y_t,1-Y_t) has eigenvalues in [3/4,5/4] and expectation I. Its operator norm is 1+|Y_t|. At every t>0 the stopped value is nonzero with positive probability, hence expected norm>1.
verdicts.remaining_gap: It is a generic matrix martingale; no assertion that it is a log-concave localization covariance. The optional small-drift extension is excluded from this KEEP pending a separately stated interval bound.

verdicts.subject: w349 WEIGHTED_GAP.md posterior factorization counterexample
verdicts.exact_scope: X=Exp(1)-1, s>0, Y=sX+sqrt(s)Z, independent standard Gaussian Z, fixed f(x)=x. Mathematical strictness only; the reported quadrature value is not independently certified by w350.
verdicts.independent_reproduction: The posterior is N((y-1)/s,1/s) truncated at -1. At y=1-s its variance is (1-2/pi)/s; as y tends to positive infinity it tends to 1/s. The variance A(y) is continuous, so it is nonconstant. Y has positive density everywhere and 0<A<=1/s, hence Var(A(Y))>0. The proposed bound reduces to E A^2 <= (E A)^2 and is strictly false.
verdicts.remaining_gap: Does not refute the correctly weighted bound or KLS.

verdicts.subject: w349 WEIGHTED_GAP.md conditional Gronwall reduction
verdicts.exact_scope: Full-dimensional compactly supported isotropic log-concave prior; smooth f; assumed uniform T>0 and K>=0 with E|Cov_mu_t(f,X)|^2 <= K E Var_mu_t(f) for almost every t<T.
verdicts.independent_reproduction: Innovation Y_t-integral a_r dr has zero conditional drift and bracket tI; compact support gives integrability, so Levy identifies a Brownian motion. Bayes/Ito gives d(mu_t f)=Cov_mu_t(f,X).dW_t. Ito isometry and total variance give V(t)=V(0)-integral E|Cov|^2. The assumed inequality implies V(T)>=exp(-KT)V(0). Posterior curvature T gives V(T)<=energy/T by generalized strong-log-concavity Poincare. For extension, truncate an arbitrary prior on expanding balls and whiten. Its means converge to 0 and covariance matrices Sigma_j converge to I; transfer the bound to the unwhitened conditional laws with factor ||Sigma_j||, then pass compact smooth tests to the limit.
verdicts.remaining_gap: The weighted all-function input and the generalized strong-log-concavity Poincare inequality are explicit external inputs; no parent proof is claimed.
